method: desk research from public first-person merchant accounts; no interviews conducted

accounts.title: How can I handle chargeback fraud after a partial refund?
accounts.evidence_type: self-reported merchant account, not independently verified transaction data
accounts.paraphrase: The author reports a two-item order, an initial partial refund, a later return of the remaining item and a chargeback for the original total. They describe assembling a timeline and difficulty resolving the refund overlap.
observed_workflow_details: dispute amount differs from remaining order value
excluded_inferences: the reported bank accounting is independently verified
the same issue occurs at the same rate for Stripe users
accounts.product_implication: Reconcile order, refund and dispute amounts separately. Report ledger uncertainty instead of recommending another refund automatically.
accounts.research_status: source re-read 6 October 2026; amounts and sequence confirmed ($500 refunded, $900 charged back, $1,400 reported loss)

accounts.title: Won chargeback without submitting evidence?
accounts.evidence_type: self-reported merchant account, not independently verified provider state
accounts.paraphrase: The author reports uploading evidence while waiting for a customer reply, then receiving a favourable outcome notification without manually submitting. They are unsure whether the customer withdrew the dispute and how that affects a promised partial refund.
observed_workflow_details: provider outcome arrives during the wait
excluded_inferences: uploaded evidence was reviewed by the bank
Stripe and Shopify have identical submission behaviour
accounts.product_implication: Keep staged evidence separate from submitted evidence. Refresh provider state on a late outcome event and invalidate obsolete action approvals.
accounts.research_status: page not retrievable at capture or on re-check (6 October 2026); treated as weaker evidence
